claims.value: A founding participant in the North Atlantic Treaty collective-defence alliance alongside the other founding states.

scope.description: Documented inter-state treaty relationship; does not imply merged sovereignty, uniform borders or currency issuer.

evidence.locator: 1949 – The 12 founding members: original signatories named; all ratified within five months. Historical France 1966 military-command withdrawal is distinguished from alliance membership.
evidence.note: Official institutional account identifies parties and historical relationship; selected interval conservatively excludes transition years.

qualifications: Related entities list the Western/Northern European founding partners represented in this research batch; Canada, Italy and the United States are also founding parties but not enumerated here.
No assertion that all members have identical armed forces or military-command participation.

claims.value: Participated in the Latin Monetary Union with Belgium, Switzerland and Italy, coordinating national coin standards.

scope.description: Documented inter-state treaty relationship; does not imply merged sovereignty, uniform borders or currency issuer.

evidence.locator: Latin Monetary Union (1865–1926): official institutional history identifies France, Italy, Switzerland, Belgium and Greece among participating countries.
evidence.note: Official institutional account identifies parties and historical relationship; selected interval conservatively excludes transition years.

qualifications: Monetary agreement, not a merged state or common sovereign currency issuer.
Interval bounded conservatively before dissolution; no assertion that convertibility and practical monetary operation remained unchanged throughout.

Related IDs enumerate Belgium and Switzerland only; the existing Italian framework IDs do not cover the entire claim interval, so Italy remains a sourced literal name without an invented target. Greece is a later participant.

claims.value: Participated with Sweden and Norway in the Scandinavian Monetary Union; member-country coins circulated as legal tender on the same basis as domestic coins.

scope.description: Documented inter-state treaty relationship; does not imply merged sovereignty, uniform borders or currency issuer.

evidence.locator: 1875 section: Denmark and Sweden established union 1873; Norway joined 16 October 1875; union functioned until 1914.
evidence.note: Official institutional account identifies parties and historical relationship; selected interval conservatively excludes transition years.

qualifications: Separate national currencies and monetary institutions remained.
Norway retained its constitutional institutions while sharing a crown with Sweden; this is not an attribution to one undifferentiated Sweden–Norway currency/state.
